rogue.summary: The mantle is now skinned. The cap over each shoulder follows the upper arm, and the collar and the front and back panels stay on the chest. In attack2 and victory, the upper arms stay under the mantle. The dagger blades are now about 30 percent longer and 15 percent wider, with the same grip. The forge check shows result ok and ground ok, with a head margin of 0.3 cm.
strengths: In attack2, a raised arm lifts the mantle cap like a pauldron. The arm stays under the cloth, and the mantle does not tear.
The longer blades read as silver lines in the attack2 and victory sprites. The crossed daggers in the victory pose are clear from the front.
The hood, the face, the gold clasp, and the hem stitches still match the mockup, and all 8 clips are present.
issues: In attack2 at t = 0.32 s, the mantle cap over the raised arm still ends in a pointed flap. It looks like a small wing for about 0.2 s.

The top of the left bracer shows through the side of the mantle, also in the rest pose. In victory, the daggers go 0.9 cm into the mantle, and in the attack, the left dagger goes 0.6 cm into the sheath.
At 128 px the blades are still thin, and the old shape issues remain: the hood is very deep from the side, and the tunic is short and plain.
next: Round the mantle hem over the shoulders, so the lifted cap has no corner. Move the bracer in, or the mantle out, so the bracer stays under the cloth.
Move the victory cross pose 1 cm forward, and move the attack slash 1 cm away from the sheaths.

archer.summary: The archer matches the mockup well and now has the full hero clip set. The bow shot draws the string and releases a nocked arrow. The bow is still small and dark.
strengths: The attack draws the string back with a nocked arrow and then releases it. The shot reads clearly in the side view.
In the death clip, the archer staggers, falls on the back, and lies still. The bow drops to the floor next to the body.
The hood point, the elf ears, and the quiver with gold fletching give a clear silhouette in all 8 sprite directions.
issues: In the front view, the bow passes in front of the face while it rises and falls. The check shows a head margin of only 0.3 cm.
The bow and the lower string go 1.0 to 1.9 cm into the tunic and the belt in attack and attack2. The arrow is thin and dark and reads weakly.
The bow is still smaller and darker than the large recurve in the mockup. The hood rim is still thick, and the legs still look short.
next: Make the bow 20 percent larger and use a lighter wood color. This item from the last review is still open.
Move the bow path away from the face and the tunic in attack and attack2. The thinner hood rim from the last review is also still open.

knight.summary: The knight is very close to the mockup and now has the full hero clip set. The helmet, the red plume, the heart shield, and the red cape read clearly at 128 px.
strengths: Steel, gold, and red cloth read as clearly different materials in the model and in the sprites.
The clip set is complete: idle, walk, run, a sword slash, a shield bash, hit, death, and victory. The feet stay planted in the walk and the run.
The shield stays clear of the face at rest, and no held item passes through the head in any clip.
issues: In the victory clip, the raised sword reaches only the brow of the helmet. In the slash, the body hides the sword during the wind-up.
The rig has no knees. The legs stay stiff when he falls and lies on the ground in the death clip.

Small contacts remain: the left gauntlet goes up to 1.1 cm into the cuirass in the death and the shield bash. The helmet has ear discs only, not the cheek guards of the mockup. At 65,322 triangles, the knight is the heaviest model.
next: Add small cheek guards to the helmet.
Move the mail ring pattern into the normal map if the triangle count must go down.

wizard.summary: The wizard is a fire mage with a large red hat, a forked fire staff, and a flame in her left palm. The front matches the mockup well. The back and the staff are simpler than in the mockup. All 8 clips work, but the death clip ends in an unclear pose.
strengths: The hat has a soft wavy brim, a curled tip, a brown band, and a gold flame badge. It gives her a clear silhouette in all 8 sprite directions.
The front has the gold V trim, the belt with the red gem, the flame motifs on the coat, and the cape that flares out on both sides.
The staff cast drives the orb at the target with the full body, and the orb flares large. In the second attack, she throws the palm flame as a fireball, and in the death clip both flames go out.
issues: The back of the cape is one plain red area with only a gold hem. From the back and the side, the hat and the cape merge into one red mass, also at sprite size.
The staff is a thin straight pole with a small fork. In the mockup, the staff is a thick twisted branch that holds the orb. The palm flame is also smaller than in the mockup.

The death clip ends with the legs up and the cape as a stiff bowl under the body. She looks seated in a tub, not flat on the ground. In the walk, the long coat hides the legs, so the stride is weak from the side.
next: Add a gold flame emblem and a trim band to the back of the cape, and make the cape a darker red than the hat.
Make the staff a thicker twisted branch with a fork that wraps around the orb, and make the palm flame larger.

cleric.summary: The cleric is a dwarf battle priest with a ginger mane, a braided beard, a large cross hammer, and a holy book. The front silhouette matches the mockup, and all eight clips are done: idle, walk, run, attack, attack2, hit, death, and victory.
strengths: The front silhouette matches the mockup: the large octagonal hammer on the right, the big ginger head, and the book with gold corners on the left.
The attack is a clear overhead smash. The hammer rises behind the head, goes over the top, and hits the ground in front of the dwarf.
The death has a stagger back, a fall, and a rest on the back. The hammer and the book stay in the hands and lie on the ground.
issues: The brows point down at the center and the eyes are large and round, so the face looks stern and young. The mockup face is older and smiles.
The side braids and their rings are short and small, so they do not show in the front view. The hair and the beard are smooth, with few strand grooves.

In the attack, the right bracer goes 0.9 cm into the collar while the hammer is up. The model has 85,000 triangles, which is the highest count of the heroes. In the east and west sprites, the hair covers most of the face.
next: Raise the brows, make the eyes a little smaller, and add heavier lower lids, for an older and friendlier face.
Make the two side braids longer, with larger gold rings, and cut deeper strand grooves in the hair and the beard.

druid.summary: The druid reads as the mushroom girl at once, and all 8 clips pass the check. The staff, the apron, and the belt still differ from the mockup. At 72,196 triangles, she is the heaviest model in the set.
strengths: The large spotted cap with the cream rim and the gills gives a unique silhouette in every view and in all 8 sprites.
The face is very close to the mockup: large brown eyes, pink cheeks, a small smile, and a ginger bob.
The clip set is complete: idle, walk, run, a staff cast, a flask throw, hit, death, and victory. The cap and the lantern lag and overshoot in the hit and the victory.
issues: The staff is still thin and straight, and the lantern is small. The mockup staff is thick and gnarled, with a large lantern on a hook.
The front is plain. The apron is a flat card with one clover, and the three belt pouches and the small hip potion are too small to read.

The attacks read weakly. The staff cast is a flat thrust at hip height with no spell effect, and the thrown flask is small with no splash. At the end of the death clip, the cap stands on its rim and hides the body in the side view.
next: Make the staff thicker and gnarled, and hang a larger lantern from a hook at the top.
Make the three belt pouches and the hip potion larger, and give the apron a scalloped hem with the mushroom motif.

adventurer.summary: The adventurer is a chibi hero with a teal bandana, a red scarf, a leather harness, a short sword, a map, and a large pack with a bedroll and a lantern. It matches the mockup in the face, the clothes, the pack, and the lantern. The hair, the bedroll, and the hand that holds the map differ from the mockup. All 8 clips pass the forge check.
strengths: The face reads at 128 px in the sprites: large brown eyes with highlights, rosy cheeks, and an open smile. The red scarf, the cream shirt, the harness, and the belt match the mockup.
The pack reads from all 8 sprite directions: the teal bedroll, the brass lantern on the side, and the flap with a buckle. The silhouette is clear in every view.

The full clip set is present: idle, walk, run, attack, attack2, hit, death, and victory. The death staggers, pitches forward, and ends face down under the pack. The forge check shows result ok and ground ok.
issues: The front hair stands up in a spiky crown, but the mockup hair sweeps to one side. At the back and the sides, the hair is one smooth mass, like a helmet.
In the attack wind-up (t = 0.2 to 0.3 s), the head and the pack hide the sword in the three-quarter and side views. The blade passes only 0.3 cm from the head.
The legs stay straight in every clip. The death fall tips the body forward as one rigid piece, and the attack2 lunge has no knee bend.
next: Add knee bones, so the run, the attack2 lunge, and the death fall bend the legs.
Sculpt the front hair to sweep to one side as in the mockup, and add separate locks to the back and the sides of the head.

goblin-warrior.summary: The goblin warrior stays close to the four-view mockup in every view. The hair on the crown is now one soft crest that leans back, as in the mockup. Each ear now has a slight cup and rolls 28 degrees, so its inner face looks a little upward. In the SW and SE sprites, the far ear still shows as a narrow upward point. The forge check shows result ok and ground ok.
strengths: The one soft crest replaces the three thin spikes. From the front it is a round, soft shape. From the side it leans back like a small flame.
The broad leaf ears, the angry eyes, and the fang read at once. The face reads at 128 px in the S, SW, and SE sprites.
All identity cues of the mockup are present: the nicked ear, one shoulder guard, the diagonal strap, the pouch, the wraps, and the dagger. At 30,374 triangles, the model is light.
issues: In the SW and SE sprites, the far ear still reads as a narrow point above the head. The raised camera looks along the ear, and the head hides the wide base of the ear.
The belt buckle is still smaller than the large tan buckle in the mockup.
The pouch is at the front of the hip, so it does not show from the back as in the mockup. The brows are thicker than the thin brows of the mockup.
next: Turn the ears more to the front (about 20 degrees of sweep instead of 32), or let the tips droop a little. Then compare the front silhouette with the mockup again.
Make the belt buckle about 30 percent larger.

horned-boar.summary: The horned boar is rebuilt in the chibi style from a new mmx mockup. It is all head and shoulders: a huge angry head, a pink snout, upturned tusks, and cream horns.
strengths: The eyes, the horns, the tusks, and the pink snout read in all eight sprite directions.
The black brows slope down toward the snout, so the face reads as angry but cute.
It keeps everything the bench brief asks for: tusks, a bristle mane, glowing eyes, and the walk, charge, and idle clips. It also has a new gore attack.
It is light: 26,188 triangles.
issues: From the side, the head looks smaller than in the mockup, because the snout is short in profile.
The horns are thinner at the tips than the thick crescents in the mockup.
The small teeth show only as a row under the snout. The mockup shows a wider open grin.
next: Make the snout 20 percent longer so that the head reads larger from the side.
Thicken the horn tips.

goblin-archer.summary: The goblin archer has its full clip set: idle, walk, run, a bow shot, hit, and death. The shot is now a real bow shot. The goblin nocks an arrow, pulls the string back to the chin, holds, and releases. The hood, the ears, the face, and the leather gear match the mockup.
strengths: The pointed dark hood with the ears through it gives a strong, unique silhouette in every view and in every sprite direction.
The shot reads. The string bends back to the right fist, a nocked arrow shows from the nock to the release, and the string snaps straight when the arrow goes.
The bow cants its top out to the right, so the upper limb stays beside the face. Both eyes stay clear in the front and three-quarter views at full draw.
issues: The short arms and the big hood keep the draw short and low. The right fist anchors under the chin, not at the jaw. In the side view, the hood and the body hide the right fist.
The ears are thin flat plates. In the side views and in the W and E sprites, they read as flat triangles. In the SW and SE sprites, they read as thin sticks.
The model differs from the mockup. It has no long back cape and no chest strap, and the nose is a small bump, not a snout. In the draw, the lower string touches the capelet by 0.9 cm.
next: Give the ears thickness and a cupped inner face, as in the mockup. Then the ears read as ears from the side and from above.
Add the long back cape and the chest strap from the mockup, and keep the lower bowstring clear of the capelet in the draw.

skeleton.summary: The skeleton warrior matches the enemy-sheet design: a grinning skull with glowing eyes under a riveted helmet, a red scarf, mail, a sword, and a round red shield. It now has the full clip set: idle, walk, run, attack, hit, and death. The forge check shows result ok and ground ok. The helmet is still dark iron, and the chop stops at the impact.
strengths: The death clip tells a clear story. The skeleton staggers, its knees buckle, and it folds into a heap. Then the helmeted skull rolls off beside the body, and the sword and the shield fall flat.
In the chop, the flat of the blade faces sideways, so the edge leads down through the cut. The wind-up now goes up and back over the right shoulder.
The slanted black sockets, the amber eyes, and the square teeth make a clear angry skull face. Iron, mail, bone, red cloth, wood, and brass read as different materials.
issues: The chop is a real sword cut only in part. The edge leads, but the huge helmet hides the raised blade in the three-quarter and side views, and the tip stays below the helmet crown. The blade stops at waist height and holds, so there is no follow-through.

The helmet is still dark iron all over. The mockup shows lighter steel with dark patches. From above, the dark dome is the largest shape in the sprites, and the face shows only in the three front directions.
The model stands in a neutral pose, but the mockup shows a lunge. The mockup has brown leather boots; the model has plain steel feet. The sword passes 0.3 cm from the head in the check.
next: Make the helmet steel lighter, with the patina in patches. This item from the old review is still open.
Lift the sword tip above the helmet crown in the wind-up, and continue the cut down past the waist before the recovery. The old item for a higher wind-up is open in part.

orc-warrior.summary: The orc warrior is a stocky brute with a heavy scowl, tusks, a topknot, a spiked pauldron, and a large crescent axe. The tusks now start under the upper lip and hang down past the lower lip, so they read as teeth from the mouth. The axe stays clear of the head in all clips, but the axe head goes into the floor in the attack and the run.
strengths: The tusks now come from the mouth. In the front view and in the S sprite, they show as two clear white teeth below the yellow eyes and the heavy brows.
The costume matches the mockup: large brown bracers, a spiked pauldron, a belt with a round buckle, a ragged red loincloth, and fur leg wraps.
The death reads well at game size: a stagger back, a fall onto the back, and the axe on the floor next to the hand.
issues: The clip check fails the ground test. The axe head goes 14.3 cm into the floor at the attack impact and 2.4 cm in the run.
The attack is a two-hand chop in name only. The left fist stays away from the haft for the full swing, so the chop reads as a one-hand swing.
The tusks are small: about half the size of the mockup tusks. They hang down from under the upper lip, as the owner asked. The beard is a small goatee, and the mockup beard is full.
next: Stop the axe head at the floor at the attack impact and in the run, so the check ends with ground ok.
Put the left hand on the haft from the wind-up to the impact, so the chop reads as a two-hand swing.

bandit.summary: The bandit has its full clip set: idle, walk, run, a cutlass slash, hit, and death. The model matches the mockup: wild dark hair, an angry glare over a dark red mask, a striped shirt, a leather vest, a loot sack, and a curved cutlass. The death reads well. The slash is the weakest clip, because the wind-up is low and short.
strengths: The glare between the dark hair and the red mask is a strong focal point. It reads in the front view and in the S, SW, and SE sprites.
The death reads well. The bandit staggers, falls on its back, and lies flat with the face up. The cutlass drops from the hand and lies on the floor.
The slash has the three parts of a real cutlass cut: a wind-up, a cut with the edge leading, and a follow-through down and across the body. The sack and the mask tails swing late.
issues: The slash is a real cut, but a weak one. In the wind-up, the hand rises only to chest height, and the blade stays upright next to the shoulder. At the strike, the blade is level at waist height, so the cut reads as a flat sweep. The step into the cut is small.

The gear is plainer than the mockup. The mockup has straps on the vest, a holster at the belt, and tall boots with cuffs. The model has a plain vest and short boots. The sack still sits behind the arm.
The cutlass passes only 0.3 cm from the head in one clip (the check head margin). The check passes, but a small change to a clip can make it fail.
next: Make the slash stronger. Lift the hand above the shoulder and hold the blade back, then cut on a diagonal from high to the opposite hip. Make the forward step longer. Keep the head margin at 1 cm or more.
Add the mockup gear: a vest strap with a buckle, a holster at the belt, and cuffs on the boots. Move the sack a little to the side. These items from the last review are still open.

zombie.summary: The zombie now has the full clip set: idle, walk, run, attack, hit, and death. The silhouette, the colors, and the mismatched eyes match the mmx mockup. The hair, the shirt, and the trouser hems are still simpler than the mockup.
strengths: The bulging yellow eye and the glossy black eye read in every sprite direction that shows the face.
The death clip reads clearly. The head snaps back, the knees give way, and the body falls forward and lies flat. Nothing goes below the ground.
The walk and the run drag one foot and keep the arms forward, so the motion reads as a zombie at once.
issues: The hair is still a smooth black helmet with thick cone locks. The mockup hair is thinner and messier. In the back sprites, the hair is a large, plain black mass.

The shirt is still plain, with no torn collar, buttons, or loose threads. The trouser tears are still paint, and the sandals are flat planks. The collar and hem threads from the last review are still open.

The attack reads as a two-hand claw, and the forward pitch of the head and the chest gives it weight. But the reach is short: the hands rise only to the ears, the strike stops at belly height, and the feet stay planted.
next: Make the hair locks thinner and more varied, and break up the smooth mass at the back. This item from the last review is still open.
Add a lunge step to the attack, and extend the arms so that the claws reach past the face at chest height.

slime.summary: The slime is the slime king from the enemy sheet without its crown, cape, and chain: a glossy green jelly with a head dome on a wider belly, a puddle of round drips, and three bubbles that float around it.
strengths: The face reads at 128 px: big white eyes with lime irises, heavy jelly brow ridges with a dark crease, and a bold, wide frown.
Three bubbles float on their own bones, and blisters bulge from the belly and the back. The side and back views are no longer a plain dome.
The motion is strong squash and stretch: a body slam with a low hold, a tall leap, and a flat splat, a squashed hit recoil, and a death that melts into a puddle while the bubbles pop.
issues: The jelly is opaque. A see-through test hid the ground shadow and showed sorting errors, so the inner bubbles are only paint.
A vertical gloss highlight runs down the middle of the face in the front view and can read as a small nose.
Without the crown, the top of the dome is still a plain round shape.
next: Make the fire, ice, and poison variants: change only the SLIME constant.
Add a spit or a split attack as a special clip.

dire-wolf.summary: The dire wolf matches the mmx mockup: a huge scowling head with cream brows, amber eyes, and a toothy grin, framed by cheek tufts, tall ears, and a full cream ruff, on a compact body with a bushy tail.
strengths: The pointed ears, cheek tufts, and ruff make a spiky outline that reads in every sprite direction.
The cream brows and muzzle around the amber eyes give a strong focal point on the dark face.
The trot moves the diagonal leg pairs together, and the bite has a clear crouch, lunge, and snap.
issues: The mockup sits in a compact crouch. The model stands on four straight legs, so the body looks longer from the side.
The fur is one smooth dark grey. The mockup fur has more value variation on the legs and the back.
The cream muzzle is still narrower than the wide grinning muzzle in the mockup.
next: Paint a slightly lighter grey on the chest and the lower cheeks.
Widen the cream muzzle toward the cheeks.

giant-spider.summary: The giant spider now has a head that tilts up 14 degrees and six small white eyeballs with red irises, as in the mockup. The full clip set is done, and no clip puts a foot or a leg below the ground.
strengths: The front view is close to the mockup: the heavy brow, the glaring red eyes, the pale fangs, the orange splat, and the white eyeballs on top.
The attack reads as a spider strike: it rears up, the front legs rise wide, then it lunges, the fangs close, and the front feet stay planted.
The death reads clearly: a recoil, the legs curl in, and it rolls onto its back with the curled legs in the air.
issues: The big abdomen sits behind the head, not under it as in the mockup. This change is on purpose, but the side view is less like the mockup.
At the end of the death, the body rests on the small eyes. The carapace stays 2.6 cm above the ground.
The big eyes show more red iris and less white than the mockup, and the body is one smooth fuzz texture.
next: Pitch the body a little at the end of the death, so the abdomen also touches the ground.
Make the big eyes whiter with a smaller red iris, as in the mockup.

dragon-fire.summary: The fire dragon matches the mmx mockup closely: a squat red dragon that is half head, with cream horns, a red and orange crest, heavy black brows, a toothy grin, spread orange bat wings, a ridged cream belly, and a finned tail.
strengths: The spread wings, horns, and crest make a unique silhouette that reads in all eight sprite directions.
The black brows over the yellow eyes and the white teeth in the dark grin give a strong focal point.
The roar reads well: it rears back with the wings raised, then lunges with the wings flared.
It has a fly clip: the body lifts and tilts forward, the wings beat through a full stroke, the legs dangle back, and the tail waves.
issues: The mockup puffs smoke from one nostril. The model has no smoke or fire effect yet.
The horns are thinner than the big cream horns in the mockup.
The cheek frills are small and hide behind the wings from the front.
next: Add a fire-breath effect as a separate effects asset, and play it with the roar.
Make the horns 20 percent thicker at the root.

blacksmith.summary: The blacksmith matches the mmx mockup: a burly smith with a black beard and a red bandana, a leather bib apron with brass rings and a buckled belt, big leather gloves, and a hammer resting on his shoulder.
strengths: The red bandana and black beard frame a friendly face that reads at 128 px in every direction.
The bib apron with straps, brass rings, and buckle reads as a smith's apron at once.
The work clip lifts the hammer and brings it down in front, onto an unseen anvil.
issues: He uses the rogue's large head, so he is less burly than the mockup, where the body is bigger than the head.
The short hair at the back of the head is one plain black mass.
In the work clip, the wind-up hides the hammer behind the head, so the lift reads weakly.
next: Make the chest and arms 10 percent bigger, so he reads as the strongest villager.
Raise the hammer higher in the wind-up of the work clip.

farmer.summary: The farmer matches the mmx mockup: a wide woven straw hat, a straw bundle in his mouth, rosy cheeks, a red plaid shirt, patched blue overalls with brass buttons, boots, and a tall pitchfork.
strengths: The wide straw hat and the upright pitchfork make a silhouette that reads as a farmer at once.
The red plaid and the blue denim are two clear color masses, with the straw hat as a light accent.
The work clip digs the fork into the ground in front and then lifts it high.
issues: From above, the wide hat hides much of the face in the sprites.
The mockup hat has a softer, floppier brim that tilts. The model brim is flat and even.
The hair shows as a smooth mass under the hat at the back.
next: Tilt the hat back a few more degrees, so the face shows more in the top-down sprites.
Give the brim a gentle wave.

guard.summary: The town guard matches the mmx mockup in form. He has a kettle helmet with a crest, a brown mustache, and a blue tabard with a gold tower over mail. He also has steel pauldrons, steel gauntlets, and a spear with a teal swallowtail pennant. He has idle, walk, run, attack (a spear thrust), hit, death, and salute (a fist to the chest). The face and the colors still differ from the mockup.
strengths: The kettle helmet with the crest, the gold tower on the tabard, the belt with the gold buckle, and the teal swallowtail pennant match the mockup.
The face reads at 128 px in the S, SW, and SE sprites. The large eyes, the brows, and the brown mustache are clear under the brim.
The thrust drives the spear straight along the shaft with a step and a forward lean, holds it, and brings it back upright. The pennant trails under the level haft.
issues: The nose is small, and the mustache is flat and wide. The mockup has a large round nose and mustache tips that curl up. The steel is bright silver (#9aa0a8), not gunmetal, and the tabard is sky blue (#6aa2c0), not teal blue.

The thrust drives straight along the shaft and recovers, but the draw back is only 2.5 cm, so it does not show. One hand holds the spear. The salute reads: the fist stops on the chest over the gold tower, but the forearm stays inside the body outline.
In the run, the spear butt goes 2.3 cm below the ground at phase 0.65 to 0.82, so the ground check fails. The right vambrace goes 0.4 cm into the tabard in the attack and the death.
next: Fix the clips. Keep the spear butt above the ground in the run at phase 0.65 to 0.82. Make the draw back in the thrust about 10 cm.

Make the nose larger and rounder, and curl the mustache tips up. Darken the steel toward gunmetal (about #70767e), and move the tabard toward teal blue (about #4a93a6). These items are still open from the last review.

skeleton-mage.summary: The skeleton mage matches the candle-skull caster on the mockup. The white wax now shows apart from the cream skull. The cast has an anticipation, a thrust toward the target, and a recovery. In the death, the mage staggers back, falls to the knees, drops the staff, and lies on its side. All clips pass the head check (margin 0.3 cm) and the ground check. The model has 43,126 triangles.
strengths: The candle on the skull is a unique silhouette. It shows clearly in all 8 sprite directions.
Three glowing accents (the candle flame, the palm flame, and the lantern) make the mage easy to see in a dark dungeon.
The death is clear: a stagger back, a fall to the knees, the staff falls to the floor, and the body lies on its side.
issues: The cast shows a real spell: the hand pulls back to the chest, then pushes the flame forward, then returns. But the palm flame keeps its size, and no bolt leaves the hand.
The known flaw is visible: after the death, the orange eyes stay lit on the skull on the floor. The candle flame also stays lit.
The candle is a wide block with a flat top, and the skull has no hood. The mockup has a taller, rounder candle and a dark hood. At 128 px, the wax drips cover part of the eye sockets.
next: At the release of the cast (phase 0.5), scale up the palm flame and make it brighter, or send a short purple bolt toward the target.
Put the eye glow on its own bone and scale it to zero at the end of the death. Scale the candle bone to zero there too.

imp.summary: The imp matches the imp on the Chibi Quest enemy sheet: a big-headed little red devil with curved dark horns, amber eyes under angry brows, a fanged grin, scalloped bat wings, clawed hands and feet, and an arrow-tipped tail.
strengths: The spread bat wings and curved horns make a spiky silhouette that reads in all eight sprite directions.
It is a true flyer: the idle hovers with beating wings, the fly clip leans into forward flight, and the attack rears and dives.
Many sharp points (horns, ears, fangs, claws, wing fingers, tail spade) make it read as dangerous, while the big head keeps it cute.
issues: In the rest pose it stands on the ground; the mockup shows it mid-flight. The idle clip lifts it, so this matters only for the static model.
The skin, the wings, and the membranes are all similar reds, so the materials separate only a little.
The mockup wings have a thick dark leading edge; the model's wing bones are thinner.
next: Make the wing's leading bone thicker and darker.
Darken the membranes toward the wing tips.

skeleton-archer.summary: The skeleton archer keeps the identity of its mmx mockup: a green hood, glowing orange eyes, a bare ribcage, red wraps, a quiver, and a bow. The attack is a full bow-shot sequence, but the draw hand stops at the chest, not at the jaw. The head check passes (margin 0.3 cm). The ground check fails, because the hidden arrow goes 4.2 cm below the ground in the attack. The model has 66,696 triangles.
strengths: The costume matches the mockup: the green hood with a ragged mantle, the ribcage with a diagonal strap, the brown loincloth with a brass buckle, the red wraps, and a quiver with red fletching.
The attack has a full sequence: the archer takes an arrow from the quiver, nocks it, points the bow arm at the target, holds with a tremble, and releases with a bow kick.
The death is clear and stays above the ground: a stagger, a fall forward, the hooded skull rolls to the front, and the bow lies flat on the ground.
issues: The shot reads as a bow shot only in part. The bow arm points at the target, and an arrow shows on the string before the release. After the release, the string is straight again. But the draw hand stops at the chest under the chin (ANCHOR y = 0.40 m), inside the mantle edge. It does not come to the jaw beside the face, and the hood hides it in the side view.

The ground check fails: in the attack, the hidden nocked arrow goes 4.2 cm below the ground at phase 0.88. The body clips from the last review stay: the red wraps go 1.3 cm into the ribs (phase 0.23-0.85), the draw hand goes 0.6 to 0.8 cm into the mantle, and the bracer goes 0.8 cm into the mantle.

The model differs from the mockup: the bow is a thin, upright stick at the side, not a recurve across the body. The hood is a smooth dome, not a draped hood. The skull is wide and flat, and the teeth are still one block with cut lines. At 128 px, the back and side sprites show only the hood and the quiver.
next: Fix the ground failure: while the shot arrow is hidden (phase 0.735 to 0.9), keep its direction at the release aim, or park it at the pinch, so it never goes below y = 0.

Still open from the last review: raise the draw anchor to the right side of the jaw, in front of the mantle, and move the draw elbow and the hand path away from the ribs and the mantle, so the body clip warnings stop. The separate teeth are also still open.

giant-rat.summary: The giant rat matches its mmx mockup: a fat, hunched rat on its hind legs with huge round pink-lined ears, bulging red eyes under angry brows, a pink nose, a jagged yellow grin with buck teeth, pale head spikes, gray back tufts, a red neckerchief, and a long ringed tail with a bandage.
strengths: The round ears, the head spikes, the back tufts, and the long tail give a clear silhouette from every side.
The white eyes with red irises and the pink nose on the cream muzzle read at 128 px in the front sprites.
The walk is a side-to-side waddle, and the attack raises the claws beside the head, then lunges into a bite and a rake.
issues: In the side view the snout is shorter and flatter than the mockup, so the profile is less pointed.
The body stands more upright than the mockup; the mockup leans forward with the head ahead of the belly.
The belly and the fur are smooth; the mockup has a wrinkled belly and shaggier fur.
next: Push the snout and the nose 0.03 m forward, and lean the chest and the head forward a little.
Add fur clumps in the bump along the sides and a few belly folds in the paint.

giant-bat.summary: The giant bat matches its mmx mockup: a round, shaggy purple fur ball with huge pointed ears, glaring yellow eyes under heavy brows, a pink pig snout, an open grin with two long fangs, pink-membraned wings on dark bones, and tiny pink feet.
strengths: The combed fur spikes give the ball a shaggy outline, and the wide pink wings and tall ears make a clear flying silhouette.
The yellow eyes with dark pupils, the pink snout, and the white fangs read in the front sprites.
The wings flap on two bones each, so the tips lag the beat; the attack rises, then dives forward with a squash.
issues: The ears are tall triangles; the mockup ears are rounder, with a wavy rim.
The fur is 32,000 of the 48,700 triangles; a reduced real-time model will need a smoother fur shell with the spikes in the normal map.
From the side, the wings show as thin pink fins beside the ball.
next: Round the ear outline and add two or three scallops to its back edge.
Angle the wings 20 degrees toward the front at rest, so the side view shows more membrane.

mimic.summary: The mimic matches its mmx mockup and is built from the treasure chest asset: the same planks, iron, lid, and gold lock, with the lid open as a jaw of big white fangs, glowing yellow slit eyes under the lid, red flesh inside, a fat purple tongue over the front, and iron claw feet.
strengths: Closed (the first frame of the reveal clip), it matches the real treasure chest, so the trap works in a level.
The white teeth and the yellow eyes on the dark mouth read in every front and three-quarter sprite.
Four clips cover the whole encounter: reveal (rattle, then spring open), idle, a waddle walk, and an attack that opens wide, lunges, and slams shut.
issues: The mockup shows gold and cloth among the flesh inside; the model has only flesh.
The teeth are straight cones; the mockup teeth are thicker at the base and curve more.
The chest body is square; the mockup chest flares out a little toward the top.
next: Add a few gold coins and a gem in the flesh, from the chest's treasure heap.
Thicken the tooth bases and bend the middle teeth a little toward the front.

animated-armor.summary: The animated armor matches its mmx mockup: a huge round great helm with a brass band, a black visor with two cyan eyes, and a slotted face plate. The dark suit has rust specks, a purple scarf, a torn cape, and a broad sword held low. It has the full enemy clip set: idle, walk, run, attack, hit, and death. The model did not change since the last review. The head check gives result ok, but the ground check fails: in the run, the sword goes into the floor.
strengths: The two cyan eyes on the black visor read at once, also in the 128 px sprites. Nothing inside the helm shows that the suit is empty.

The slash reads as a real sword cut. The blade rises up and back beside the helm and holds, then cuts across the front with the edge first (edgeUp). The follow-through ends low at the left, and the hips and chest turn with it.
The death tells the story: the eyes flicker out, the sword drops flat, the helm falls off in front and rolls onto its side, and the legs splay.
issues: In the run, the sword goes 7.0 cm below its rest pose in every frame, and the tip cuts into the floor (ground FAIL). The hips drop and the spine leans 10 degrees, but the right arm does not lift the blade.

In the attack, the top of the backswing is behind the helm in the front view, so the front sprite shows mainly the follow-through. From phase 0.58 to 0.75, the right gauntlet goes 0.7 cm into the cuirass. At the end of the death, the cape stands out as a stiff, flat panel above the ground.
The helm is a smooth round dome. The mockup helm has a raised brow over the visor and cheek plates that flare out. The rust specks on the helm dome and the pauldrons are still small and sparse.
next: Lift the sword in the run, so that it stays less than 1.5 cm below its rest pose and ./forge check gives ground ok. Then lay the death cape flat on the ground, and keep the right forearm 1 cm clear of the cuirass in the attack.
Give the helm a raised brow ridge over the visor, and add more rust and scratches on the helm dome and the pauldrons. Both items from the last review are still open.
